💡 Key Takeaways
  • Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.
  • On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.
  • It has been revealed that circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

It has been revealed that circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

Recent findings suggest that most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Recent findings suggest that embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It indicates: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

Sources indicate that the schedule is fixed. Circle confirmed in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026.".

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide states "message limits will tighten over time until no new burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the company wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible.".

Funds already in transit are protected. The guide says "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations.".

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1.".

The main text above it notes something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:.

Circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

As of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle said "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:.

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small concern, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or revision integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

The fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:.

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

For Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

For everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG company that builds on Bittensor.

Recent findings suggest that at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert noted that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson stated.

Recent findings suggest that the gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

The November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

Recent findings suggest that SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

According to recent reports, TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Recent findings suggest that shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it. “You come as a problem solver, not a fan,” he noted.

Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.

Sangaré came to the U.S. when he was hired to work for Tony Parker, his former teammate, in San Antonio, Texas; he started as a financial advisor for professional athletes. During COVID, he moved into real estate, specializing in finding homes for athletes instead.

Recent findings suggest that sangaré explains that the pros tend to make a lot of money for a short period of time, and for that reason they’re usually interested in buying investment properties (often right after they’ve found homes for themselves and their family members). A big part of their real estate agents’ job, then, is to keep their eyes on investment properties with the potential for strong returns.

Sources indicate that athletes have specific needs. “As a rookie, they’re just starting out, and they may not want to buy,” Sangaré told Taylor Anderson at eXpcon in Salt Lake City last month. Depending on the length of the contract, a rental might be a better idea. “There are times you tell people now’s not the right time to buy. If they feel you’re working in their best interests, they will trust you,” noted Sangaré, who is part of eXp’s relatively new sports and entertainment division (which several brokerages offer).

Sources indicate that you have to be patient when working with athletes, he noted, since their situations are tied to ever-changing contracts; of course, players can be traded, and have to move quickly. You also have to be prepared to wait and work with them as they grow in their careers.

It has been revealed that what you don’t have to be: A major follower of their particular sports. Sangaré admits that as a European, he doesn’t know much about football or baseball, but that doesn’t stop him from working with athletes in those sports. Sometimes not being starstruck helps him work with a more level head, he said.

It has been revealed that but you do need to know the nuances of sports contracts. For example, some leagues, like the NBA, offer several-year guarantees, while others, like the NFL, don’t; housing options will vary based on those.

Often the connection to an athlete client comes through their financial advisor or sports agent, Sangaré stated. “The sports agent is always talking to the player, and he’ll know to reach out to you when someone gets traded,” he said.

Sources indicate that but that can be a long road. Sangaré noted it can take anywhere from five months to two years from starting a relationship with a sports agent to seeing any traction with a player, but you want to start that relationship early since once their clients do start to get traded, they’ll undoubtedly be approached by many other real estate agents. One practical tip he gives is going to the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas and taking agents out for coffee or lunch. “You have to be present where they’re present,” he said.

And when you do get connected to the client, make sure you don’t start with a sales pitch. “You can’t try to sell them something right away,” Sangaré mentioned; instead, you want to counsel them on how they can protect themselves and what they really need to know when buying a home — whether as an investment property or to live in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest release strengthens multi-turn tool use and long-horizon task execution within the same compact footprint.

Industry observers note that PASADENA, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PrismML today announced Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to the Ternary Bonsai 2 27B with substantially stronger agentic coding and multi-turn tool use. The model is based on Qwen3.8 27B, sits at 5.9GB memory, and retains or exceeds the benchmark scores of its predecessor, giving developers a strong foundation for coding and knowledge work agents that run on personal devices.

It has been revealed that across agentic coding benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, DeepSWE v1.1, and Terminal-Bench 2.1), Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B achieved an average score of 54.2, compared to 37.9 for Ternary Bonsai 2 27B. Across agentic tool-calling benchmarks (AppWorld and ÏÂ³-Bench), Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B achieved an average score of 82.2, compared to 60.2 for Ternary Bonsai 2 27B. Full results and evaluation settings are available in the accompanying whitepaper.

Preserving capability across longer tasks.

Agentic workloads are particularly demanding for compressed models. Small errors can compound across successive tool calls, causing an agent to lose track of its objective or repeat unsuccessful approaches. Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B addresses these limitations, significantly narrowing the performance gap to the full-precision model on longer, multi-step tasks.

Industry observers note that development focused on how the model responds as a task unfolds: incorporating tool feedback, recovering from failed actions, and avoiding unnecessary reasoning and unproductive repetition. The goal is to help agents complete work more reliably, with fewer wasted steps, lower token use, and shorter execution times.

Recent findings suggest that "Getting a capable model onto a device is only part of the challenge," said Babak Hassibi, Founder and CEO of PrismML. "It also has to remain effective through all the decisions involved in completing a real complex task. That is where we focused our work with Bonsai 2.5.".

From private codebases to everyday knowledge work.

The release expands the scope of work developers can build local agents to handle. A coding assistant can inspect a private repository, make changes, run the relevant tests, and use the results to refine its fix, all within the developer's local environment. A knowledge work assistant can turn a folder of documents into a structured analysis, reconcile inconsistent records, or prepare a repeatable workflow for recurring reports. These assignments require sustained execution across files and tools. Stronger performance over longer interactions makes more of this work practical to delegate.

For product teams, this makes it easier to embed capable agents directly into their applications, using existing context and tools while keeping model inference and sensitive information on the user's device. PrismML also works with developers on domain-specific post-training and inference optimization to tailor these capabilities to their applications and target hardware.

Industry observers note that ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B uses ternary weights to deliver 27B-class capabilities in a compact 5.9 GB model footprint. It runs on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs through llama.cpp and on Apple devices, including Mac, iPhone, and iPad, through MLX.

Technical details of PrismML's compression, evaluation, and benchmarking processes are available in the manufacturer's whitepaper.

Developers, researchers, and other users can download the Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B model under the Apache 2.0 license for free starting November 24, 2026.

Sources indicate that we work with teams to tailor Bonsai models to their applications, from post-training on domain-specific data to optimizing inference for target hardware. If you're building AI products with tight memory, latency, or power requirements, we'd love to explore how Bonsai can help. Reach out at [email protected].

UPDATED 12:19 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

It has been revealed that cloudera Inc. today confirmed a digital sovereignty package that it remarked enables organizations to maintain control over their data, artificial intelligence models and computing infrastructure regardless of where workloads run.

Cloudera for Digital Sovereignty combines the firm’s Anywhere Cloud, Open Data Lakehouse and Unified Data Fabric technologies with open-weight AI models and model customization tools from Mistral AI SAS, with whom Cloudera recently partnered. The integrated offering supports deployment across sovereign clouds, private data centers and fully air-gapped environments that have no connection to external networks.

In a recent development, digital sovereignty is becoming a more pressing glitch as enterprises move beyond managing data residency to ensuring that the AI models and infrastructure they depend upon remain under their control. McKinsey & Co. reported last year that 71% of the executives it surveyed called sovereign AI an “existential concern” or “strategic imperative.” Cloudera said its own research found that regulation, privacy and data sovereignty requirements rank among the top three barriers to scaling AI.

“As AI becomes more autonomous and embedded in critical operations, enterprises need to know that their data, models, and infrastructure can remain under their control even as technology and regulatory requirements change,” Cloudera Chief Technology Officer Sergio Gago said in a statement.

In a recent development, the offering provides consistent zero-trust access controls, data lineage tracking and governance policies across deployment environments. Those capabilities are intended to help organizations address requirements imposed by the European Union’s AI Act, Digital Operational Resilience Act and Network and Information Security Directive, among other regulations.

In a recent development, governance policies also extend to the enterprise data that AI agents retrieve and use in performing tasks. Mistral’s open-weight models can run alongside governed data, enabling organizations to customize models locally and execute agentic workflows without exposing sensitive information.

Cloudera’s modular hybrid cloud architecture enables users to shift computing workloads between infrastructure providers and private data centers without rewriting applications or migrating or duplicating underlying data. Organizations can also selectively apply sovereignty controls to sensitive workloads without imposing the same restrictions across their entire computing estate.

Moor Insights & Strategy Inc. Chief Analyst Patrick Moorhead noted AI has raised the bar on data protection. “A tech giant can meet every line of its sovereignty policy and still not control who accesses its data or who can turn off the models it depends on,” he said in a statement.

Industry observers note that cloudera remarked it will supplement its Mistral partnership with an ecosystem of sovereign cloud providers and implementation partners. The company is initially targeting Europe but looks to expand the partner network into other regions and regulatory jurisdictions.

#190715. Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers said no.
  • When agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds.
  • But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to price more precisely? Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers said no. Learn three steps to add failed listings to your next CMA.

When agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds. Look at what’s coming soon, active and pending. Adjust for condition, location, square footage and amenities. Figure out where our house fits.

But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.

It has been revealed that expired. Canceled. Withdrawn. Earlier in my career, I looked at these failed listings all the time. Then the market changed. When inventory became tight, and buyers were competing for homes, digging through failed listings often wasn’t necessary to determine where a property would sell.

Now the market is shifting again; pricing must be more precise, and I’m sharpening my approach by bringing an old tool back into my pricing process.

A sold comp tells us where a buyer said yes, but a failed listing can help us figure out where buyers said no. And in a buyer-favored market, that’s valuable information.

Imagine you’re pricing a home, and the recent comparable sales range from $600,000 to $625,000. Then you expand your search.

It has been revealed that suddenly, you know considerably more than the sold comps alone told you. Other sellers have already tested the upper limits of pricing, and buyers responded. It’s essentially a series of pricing experiments someone else conducted for you — and they paid the carrying costs.

One of the most interesting things buried in MLS history is the pricing journey. A property might show a final list price of $649,000 and an eventual sale of $630,000. Dig deeper, and you may discover this:.

$725,000 → $699,000 → $675,000 → canceled → relisted at $649,000 → sold for $630,000.

That’s a different story. The sale tells us what one buyer eventually paid. The listing history tells us buyers had previously rejected that house at $725,000, $699,000 and $675,000.

According to recent reports, it also illustrates something sellers don’t always understand: Getting to the right price eventually isn’t necessarily the same as pricing correctly from the beginning. After months of market exposure and multiple reductions, buyers may stop asking, “Could this be the house?” They start asking, “What’s wrong with it?”.

When I find a comparable property that sat for 90 days without selling, I want to know what did sell during those same 90 days. Sometimes we blame the market when the market was functioning just fine. Buyers were buying houses. They simply weren’t buying that one.

Maybe they chose the renovated house at $640,000. Maybe they paid $650,000 for the better lot. They may have even paid more for another property because it offered something the failed listing didn’t. That’s useful information when you’re sitting across from a seller who believes buyers just need more time to appreciate their home.

If buyers repeatedly toured the property and purchased competing homes instead, the market may already have delivered its opinion.

This is where agents have to resist oversimplifying the data. An expired listing isn’t automatic proof that a house was overpriced, and a canceled listing certainly isn’t either.

Listings fail for all sorts of reasons. Sellers change their minds. Job transfers fall through. Repairs surface. Agents get fired. Sometimes a seller receives a perfectly acceptable offer and decides not to move.

According to recent reports, so, investigate. Call the previous agent. I might simply say:.

Sources indicate that “I’m pricing a similar property and noticed yours was on the market last year. Is there anything you can tell me about the activity or why the seller decided not to continue?”.

Twenty-seven showings and no offers tell me something. Two showings in four months tells me something different.

There’s one more number worth considering: the cost of the pricing journey.

Sources indicate that find a house that started high, sat, reduced, expired, relisted and eventually sold. Then compare it with similar homes that entered the market closer to where buyers were actually buying.

Sellers often view aspirational pricing as a no-risk strategy: “We can always come down.” Technically, that’s true. But time isn’t free, and neither is market perception.

The next time you’re preparing a CMA in a shifting or buyer-favored market:.

We’re very good at studying success in real estate. But as pricing gets harder, I’ve found myself returning to an old habit: studying the failures, too. Sold listings tell us where buyers have been willing to say yes. Sometimes the house nobody bought is the one that tells us exactly where they started saying no.

Roxanne Hale is the associate broker of the Art House Team, brokered by RealtySouth in Birmingham, Alabama. Get connected on Facebook or YouTube.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Homebuyer affordability improved slightly in October as lower purchase loan amounts offset higher mortgage rates, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA)’s Purchase Applications Payment Index (PAPI), released Tuesday.
  • The index, which measures mortgage payments relative to borrower income, decreased 0.3% to a reading of 161.6 in October, down from 162.1 in September.
  • The improvement came despite the national median mortgage payment for purchase applicants rising to $2,236 in October, up $21 (or 0.9%) from $2,215 in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homebuyer affordability improved slightly in October as lower purchase loan amounts offset higher mortgage rates, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA)’s Purchase Applications Payment Index (PAPI), released Tuesday.

The index, which measures mortgage payments relative to borrower income, decreased 0.3% to a reading of 161.6 in October, down from 162.1 in September. A lower index reading indicates improving affordability.

The improvement came despite the national median mortgage payment for purchase applicants rising to $2,236 in October, up $21 (or 0.9%) from $2,215 in September. The median purchase loan application amount fell to $315,424 from $324,022, helping offset a 37-basis-point increase in mortgage rates.

“While the median mortgage payment rose $21 in October, payments as a share of earnings edged lower — slightly improving affordability,” Edward Seiler, MBA’s associate vice president of housing economics and executive director of the Research Institute for Housing America, noted in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that affordability remains weaker than a year ago. The median mortgage payment increased 9.7% from $2,039 in October 2025, while earnings grew 1.6%. As a result, the PAPI was up 8% year over year.

“Looking ahead, lower mortgage rates and stronger earnings growth would give prospective buyers more room in their budgets,” Seiler said.

According to recent reports, the median mortgage payment for Federal Housing Administration (FHA) borrowers increased to $1,944 in October, up from $1,906 in September and $1,789 a year earlier. For conventional loan borrowers, the median payment rose to $2,258, up from $2,244 in September and $2,063 in October 2025.

Among borrowers applying for lower-payment mortgages, those in the 25th percentile, the median monthly payment increased to $1,536 in October from $1,525 in September.

Sources indicate that the PAPI for Black households decreased to 162.4 in October from 162.9 in September. For Hispanic households, it fell to 149.6 from 150.1, while the index for white households declined to 162.8 from 163.3.

Industry observers note that idaho had the highest PAPI reading in October at 269.8, followed by Nevada at 243.0, Rhode Island at 233.1, Arizona at 215.2 and Utah at 202.7. At the opposite end of the spectrum, Louisiana had the lowest reading at 119.8, followed by Washington, D.C., at 121.5, Alaska at 126.2, Iowa at 127.6 and Connecticut at 131.6.

Sources indicate that the MBA’s mortgage payment-to-rent ratio also edged higher, increasing to 1.44 at the end of the third quarter from 1.43 at the end of the second quarter. The increase indicates that mortgage payments for home purchases rose slightly relative to rents.

The U.S. Census Bureau reported that the national median asking rent increased to $1,541 in the third quarter from $1,531 in the second quarter. The ratio of mortgage payments for lower-payment applicants to median asking rents remained at 0.99 in September.

Separately, the MBA’s Builders’ PAPI indicated that the median mortgage payment for new-home purchase applicants increased to $2,375 in October, up from $2,307 in September.

Mainland China public securities.

Mainland China asset management.

Mainland China asset management, operating under the Gopher Asset Management brand, is the business that manages RMB-denominated private equity funds and private secondary products. Our international operations are organized into three reportable segments: international wealth management, international asset management, and international insurance and comprehensive services. International wealth management.

International insurance and comprehensive services.

We stayed with our decision to step back from insurance distribution and put our resources into investment products and global asset allocation, where our long-term strengths lie. "This quarter's results also include several one-off costs from streamlining our organization. We see these as investments in a leaner, more focused Noah.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

It has been revealed that but a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration proposal and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It indicates how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

According to recent reports, it also notes plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

In a recent development, A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":.

It has been revealed that turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

According to recent reports, mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

In a recent development, the tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC demonstrated almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

According to recent reports, the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence reveals what that requirement means on-chain.

Recent findings suggest that so Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

According to recent reports, the second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility.
  • According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is right now facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.
  • According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is right now facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further shows that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is notable to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

At the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data demonstrates that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

Make it 8: Connecticut joins first responder homebuying push

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.
  • The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing.
  • In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.

The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing. To qualify, first responders must have completed two years of service and purchase a primary residence within the community they serve.

In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.

It has been revealed that “Connecticut’s police officers, firefighters and EMS personnel dedicate themselves to protecting our families and communities, and we want to make sure they have the opportunity to build their own futures here,” Governor Ned Lamont noted in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them.”.

The program is part of Public Act 26-12, a state bill that aims to increase the number of first responders with a number of incentives, including college tuition reimbursement and improved labor protections.

“The people who protect and serve our communities should be able to afford to live in those communities, and this program with help them do it,” Comptroller Sean Scanlon said in a written statement. “Helping the people who put their lives on the line for us every day buy their first home is literally the least we can do, and I’m proud to have worked with Governor Lamont and legislature to make this a reality.”.

Sources indicate that seven other states also have down payment assistance programs for first responders. Florida, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina provide flat amounts, ranging from $10,000 to $35,000. Texas, Maryland and Ohio’s programs are percentage-based and offer assistance ranging from 2.5 percent to 5 percent of the purchase price.

The terms of each program vary. Most states forgive the assistance after five to seven years, but Nevada requires homebuyers to repay the funds within 30 years. And like Connecticut, Ohio also offers a 0.25 percent mortgage rate discount.

Industry observers note that “Homeownership offers more than a place to live. It creates stability, strengthens connections to community and provides an opportunity to build wealth over time,” CHFA CEO and Executive Director Nandini Natarajan said in an announcement. “Through First Responders’ Time to Own, we’re helping the people who answer the call for our communities take an notable step toward achieving their own homeownership goals.”.

First responders often fall through the cracks of housing assistance programs because they don’t earn enough to afford market-rate housing but earn too much to qualify for federal housing vouchers.

According to recent reports, inman explored this dilemma last September in a feature on workforce housing in resort towns like Jackson Hole, Vail and Tahoe. These towns can’t operate without first responders and other essential workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. However, rental and for-sale home prices have far outpaced what these workers earn, forcing them to commute long distances from more affordable towns or take on second and third jobs to survive.

The solution for some of these towns has been investing in workforce housing, which caps prices for households that earn between 60 percent and 120 percent of their area’s AMI. Most workforce housing is rent-only, but some states are extending the programs to include for-sale properties.

Industry observers note that “I think the fact that workforce housing can be necessary or is a thing in the first place is really an indictment of the state of housing affordability in the country today,” Realtor.com Senior Economist Jake Krimmel mentioned. “I think it’s important to ground any conversation about workforce and affordable housing in that reality. It’s a market failure and a policy failure that someone could be a doctor, a teacher or another kind of professional and cannot afford to pay the market rent or own a home outright.”.

Windermere Principal Economist Jeff Tucker said workforce housing isn’t a panacea for affordability and works within an ecosystem of other housing and economic policies, such as upzoning, to create a more equitable market.

Sources indicate that tucker’s comments came a month after the Senate introduced the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025, and three months before the House introduced the Housing for the 21st Century Act. The bills were eventually combined into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed in June.

It has been revealed that “A broad package of necessary reforms to make more housing construction possible in much of the country is a really notable component of a long-term solution to the housing affordability challenges we face,” Tucker remarked. “Our current housing shortage took years to develop. So it’ll take years to build our way out of it.”.

#190709. Tech Report: Lower mortgage rates could bring buyers back. What market will they return to?

Tech Report: Lower mortgage rates could bring buyers back. What market will they return to?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The possibility of mortgage rates falling below 7% before the holidays is back on the table.
  • But for housing professionals hoping to reengage buyers who stepped away from the market, mortgage rates are only part of the equation.
  • The homes available, the prices sellers are asking and the competition buyers face may look considerably different from when those buyers last searched.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The possibility of mortgage rates falling below 7% before the holidays is back on the table. In Tuesday morning’s Analyst Insights update in HousingWire Intelligence, HousingWire Lead Analyst Logan Mohtashami noted that the 10-year Treasury yield had reached 4.89%, approaching the 4.85% threshold he is watching, though mortgage spreads still need to improve.

But for housing professionals hoping to reengage buyers who stepped away from the market, mortgage rates are only part of the equation.

The homes available, the prices sellers are asking and the competition buyers face may look considerably different from when those buyers last searched.

According to recent reports, nationally, active single-family inventory stands at 894,692 homes, approximately 8% higher than a year ago. New pending listings increased 5.7% in the week ending Nov. 20, while new listings increased 1.2%.

That increase in contract activity is encouraging, but the broader picture remains more complicated.

HousingWire Data shows that 44 of 57 large metro areas (77.2%) recorded an improving ratio of upcoming pending listings to new listings over consecutive four-week periods, even as pending activity remained below year-ago levels.

During the comparable period in 2025, just three of 54 qualifying metros (5.6%) indicated that same combination.

An improving relationship between incoming listings and fresh contracts does not necessarily indicate strengthening buyer demand. And if lower mortgage rates do bring buyers back, the opportunities they encounter will vary considerably by market.

Consider Denver and Kansas City, two metro areas averaging nearly identical numbers of fresh pending listings per week but offering buyers different inventory and pricing environments.

Industry observers note that over the four weeks ending Nov. 20, Denver averaged 497 fresh pending listings per week, while Kansas City averaged 491. Both markets are experiencing substantially weaker contract activity than a year ago.

That’s where the similarities begin to fade.

Denver’s housing market offers buyers a different landscape heading into the holidays, with more available inventory, lower asking prices than during the spring and widespread price reductions.

For buyers who paused their home searches earlier this year because of affordability, Denver’s changing inventory and pricing conditions provide a reason to revisit their options, even before mortgage rates move meaningfully lower.

Kansas City’s median asking price has declined from its summer peak as price reductions have become more prevalent, although median asking prices remain above year-ago levels.

Kansas City offers buyers considerably more selection than a year ago. And while asking prices have moderated since the summer, higher median asking prices compared with last year could offset some of the affordability gains from lower borrowing costs.

Both markets offer more available homes than a year ago, but the pricing environments are different.

In Denver, a decline in mortgage rates could coincide with lower asking prices and more available homes. In Kansas City, greater selection and recent pricing adjustments may create opportunities, even though the median asking price remains higher than it was a year ago.

Changes in median asking prices can reflect shifts in the composition of available inventory, not just changes in individual home prices. That’s why examining inventory, asking prices and price reductions together provides a more useful assessment of local buying conditions than any one metric alone.

Another consideration is whether contract activity is already beginning to strengthen, even with mortgage rates above 7%.

In Denver, weekly newly introduced pending listings increased across the four most recent reporting weeks:.

Cincinnati, Ohio, recorded a similar pattern, with weekly new pending listings increasing from 397 to 459 over the same period.

But Cincinnati presents a different inventory and pricing environment. Its median active list price is up 1.9% year over year, and the market has 2.44 months of inventory, compared with 3.01 in Denver.

While both markets have recorded three consecutive weekly increases in contract activity, buyers returning to Cincinnati could encounter a tighter inventory environment than those returning to Denver.

Neither market has recovered to last year’s level of contract activity, and several weeks of increases are not enough to establish a sustained recovery, particularly heading into the holidays.

It has been revealed that still, these are developments worth monitoring. If contract activity continues to strengthen while new listings decline seasonally, competition for available homes could increase.

Housing professionals don’t need to wait for mortgage rates to fall below 7% to start preparing for that possibility.

The more immediate opportunity is to understand how local market conditions have changed since buyers last evaluated their options.

For buyer’s agents: Revisit the searches of clients who paused their homebuying plans earlier this year. Has available inventory expanded in their price range? Are more homes experiencing price reductions? Changing market conditions may create opportunities worth exploring before rates move lower.

For listing agents: More available inventory means more competition for sellers. Monitor new pending listings alongside active inventory and price reductions to help sellers evaluate whether their pricing strategy remains competitive as buyer activity changes.

It has been revealed that for mortgage lenders: Reengaging prospective purchase borrowers doesn’t have to begin with a conversation about mortgage rates. Understanding how available homes and asking prices have changed in a borrower’s target market can help make that conversation more relevant. Revisit purchasing power using current local asking prices and different mortgage rate scenarios.

According to recent reports, for brokerage leaders: National mortgage rate movements can provide a reason to launch buyer reengagement campaigns, but local housing conditions should inform the messaging. A market with expanding inventory and declining asking prices presents a different opportunity than one with tighter inventory and strengthening contract activity.

Using HousingWire Intelligence, you can recreate the charts above for your own metro area, city or ZIP code.

Select single-family homes, choose the one-year view and examine four metrics together:.

Use the one-year view to understand seasonal patterns, then narrow your analysis to the most recent three or six months to identify changes in market conditions.

Looking at these metrics together can help you distinguish between a market offering greater selection and potential affordability opportunities and one where renewed buyer activity could increase competition for available homes.

Mortgage rates may give buyers a reason to reconsider their prepares. Understanding how local market conditions have changed gives housing professionals a reason to reach out before they do.

Qualifying metro areas may differ between comparison periods. New pending listings represent homes entering contract, not closed transactions. Median active list prices reflect asking prices and may be influenced by changes in the composition of available inventory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 13:50 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Australia-based Myriota Pty. Ltd., a global satellite platform for the industrial internet of things, today announced it has raised $40 million in the first portion of its Series C to launch next-generation satellites and accelerate customer adoption across international markets.

Main Sequence Ventures, Hostplus and Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation co-led the round. Funds SA joined as a newly introduced investor. The round raised the manufacturer’s total funding to more than $107.5 million, and is expected to close in early 2027.

Founded in 2015, Myriota’s platform makes satellite connectivity commercially viable for large-scale industrial IoT, using the same core technology to track mining equipment and trailers to also monitor fuel tanks, livestock water supplies and off-grid solar.

Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer’s platform combines satellite connectivity, low-power devices, field installation tools and fleet management software to support existing infrastructure. The objective is to provide access to communication tools that connect what is in place with turnkey service, so a company can connect devices, machines and smart sensors no matter how remote they are.

“We’re at the beginning of a fundamental shift in industrial IoT,” Chief Executive Ben Cade mentioned. “Industries increasingly rely on data from the field to make decisions about their operations, assets and resources, and as AI moves into the physical world, that data becomes even more essential.”.

The company expanded its platform over the past 12 months with the launch of HyperPulse, a global 5G non-terrestrial network, or NTN, and terrestrial service, and AssetHawk, a rugged, long-life asset tracker designed to make it economical to track industrial objects.

Sources indicate that alongside the expansion, it also grew into newly introduced verticals such as industrial fuels. It monitors and tracks fuel deployments across North America and Latin America, with EMEA and Asia Pacific to follow.

Sources indicate that myriota competes in a sector led by established operators such as Iridium Communications Inc., Orbcomm Inc. and Viasat Inc., alongside a growing field of providers pursuing cheaper, standards-based connections for industrial sensors and trackers.

The company mentioned it intends to use the funds to expand its space infrastructure, including developing and launching its next-generation satellites.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recognition honors Jacobsen's invention of reciprocal deposits and nearly 25 years of innovation, helping banks compete and serve their communities.

ARLINGTON, Va., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mark P. Jacobsen, Cofounder and CEO of IntraFi, was named the EY Entrepreneur Of The YearÂ® 2026 National Award winner in the Financial Services category, recognizing his pioneering contributions to the banking industry and his leadership in building the nation's largest reciprocal deposit network.

The recognition celebrates Jacobsen's contributions to helping community and regional banks attract and retain deposits, allowing them to grant access for their customers to aggregate higher levels of FDIC insurance coverage and enabling them to better serve their communities.

Nearly 25 years ago, Jacobsen recognized a challenge facing community banks and their customers. Businesses and municipalities often needed to maintain deposits exceeding traditional FDIC insurance limits, while smaller banks struggled to compete with larger institutions for those relationships.

Jacobsen "conceived the idea of reciprocal deposits," wrote EY in its recognition. "IntraFi created an entirely new banking product.".

Reciprocal deposit services allow community banks to place uninsured deposits through a deposit placement network in increments below FDIC insurance limits and receive a matching amount of insured deposits in return. This allows small businesses, public funds and nonprofits to obtain higher levels of aggregate FDIC insurance. This benefits both the bank and its customers, allowing depositors to have a single relationship with their preferred institution while the bank can use the full amount of the deposit to fuel economic growth.

"Jacobsen brought the idea to life by combining a regulator's understanding of the financial system and an entrepreneur's instinct to challenge conventional thinking, plus the resolve to see the challenge through," said EY, noting Jacobsen's former role as the chief of staff of two federal banking regulators. "He earned a dozen patents and worked with all the federal banking agencies as well as state and local governments, prompting more than 40 state laws to enable the use of reciprocal deposits.".

According to recent reports, today, IntraFi operates the nation's largest reciprocal deposit network, connecting more than 3,000 financial institutions, the vast majority of which are community banks. IntraFi's scale, sophisticated infrastructure, and proven reliability distinguish it from other providers, with established systems that have supported banks through multiple financial crises and periods of market stress.

"Any recognition belongs solely to the employees of IntraFi and the thousands of banks that have put their faith in us," remarked Jacobsen. "We built this network bank by bank with a commitment to do things the right way, not relying on marketing puffery or short-lived promises. And we remain committed to constant innovation. Whether it's helping community banks compete for deposits or exploring how our network could support the next generation of payments, our goal remains the same: giving banks the tools they need to better serve their customers.".

IntraFi's unmatched network scale and proven operational reliability reinforces its position as a trusted partner to banks of all sizes.

The EY Entrepreneur Of The Year program recognizes entrepreneurs whose innovation, leadership, and vision have transformed industries and created lasting economic and community impact.

In a recent development, intraFi has built the largest financial network of its kind, connecting thousands of financial institutions nationwide. The company is the nation's leading provider of reciprocal deposit services and a leading provider of overnight and term funding options. IntraFi helps financial institutions manage liquidity, access funding, and provide customers with solutions for keeping large deposits safe.

IntraFi is not an FDIC-insured bank, and deposit insurance covers the failure of an insured bank. A list identifying IntraFi network banks appears at https://www.intrafi.com/network-banks. Certain conditions must be satisfied for "pass-through" FDIC deposit insurance coverage to apply. Use of an IntraFi service is subject to the terms, conditions, and disclosures in the applicable program agreements.

#190704. Your real estate listing is stuck and a price drop will not fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1008 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Your real estate listing is stuck and a price drop will not fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there is a category of stuck listing that is going to become more common over the next few years, and most agents have not been trained for it.
  • This came up on one of our Power Agent coaching calls.
  • Recent findings suggest that the building had a balcony and structural-compliance issue, the kind of inspection-and-repair requirement that has spread across the country since Surfside and that states like California have written into law for decks and balconies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there is a category of stuck listing that is going to become more common over the next few years, and most agents have not been trained for it. It is the listing that cannot sell for a reason that has nothing to do with price, photography or effort. It is the listing blocked at the building level, and if we keep coaching agents to treat every slow listing with a price reduction, we are going to watch good professionals burn good listings for no reason.

This came up on one of our Power Agent coaching calls. An agent brought me a four-unit situation. The condo had been on the market for 86 days. She had lost two solid buyers. One was all cash, and the all-cash buyer still walked. Any time an all-cash buyer walks, leaders should pay attention, because the one thing you cannot blame is financing.

Recent findings suggest that the building had a balcony and structural-compliance issue, the kind of inspection-and-repair requirement that has spread across the country since Surfside and that states like California have written into law for decks and balconies. The repairs had not been started. A new management company had taken over months earlier and was still, in their words, figuring things out.

Because the work was un-started, the building landed on the list that does not qualify for conventional Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac financing. The financed buyers were gone instantly. The all-cash buyer pulled the association financials, saw thin reserves and un-started repairs, read it correctly as a poorly run building, and decided the headache was not worth it.

Powerfact: Structural-compliance problems do not lower a home’s price. They remove a home’s buyers.

Industry observers note that that distinction matters for anyone leading a team, because it changes the coaching. When a building cannot get conventional financing, the buyer pool does not shrink, it collapses to cash buyers willing to tolerate a troubled association. We just watched one of those rare buyers say no. Telling that agent to drop the price would have been coaching malpractice. The price was never the lever.

Here is the initiative I gave her, and it is the plan I would want every leader teaching.

Take it off the market, temporarily. Days on market is a public number, and a climbing one negotiates against your seller before an offer is ever written. Pull the listing before the clock becomes the story.

Industry observers note that then, stay hired. This is the step that separates an advisor from an order-taker. Taking a listing off the market should not end the relationship, it should restructure it. The agent and I built a new listing agreement long enough to cover the repair timeline plus fresh marketing afterward at a likely new price.

In a recent development, if repairs take a couple of months and the sale takes several more, that is an eight or nine month agreement, not a renewal of the old 90 days. The property comes off the MLS and is not shown, but the agreement stays active. The agent keeps her position. The seller keeps a professional who is still working.

In a recent development, then, advocate for the whole building. I told her to get in front of the management company and the association board, the president and the vice president, and push to expedite repairs that are hurting all 54 owners. This is where a top producer builds a reputation that compounds. When you are the agent pushing a stalled building back into compliance, every owner in that building knows your name, and so does every agent who tried and gave up. In a 54-unit building, that is 54 future listing conversations you just earned by being the one who indicated up and did the work nobody else would touch.

We also talked through the rent-instead question, because these sellers had already relocated and were carrying the unit. Renting for a year while the building gets sorted is a legitimate option, but it has to be coached with the worst case on the table. In a tenant-friendly jurisdiction an eviction can run six to nine months. Florida’s landlord rules are workable. Other markets are not.

This property sits in California, and I told her plainly that I do not know California’s specifics well enough to promise a timeline, so she needs to find out. Because if the tenant will not leave and removal takes six months, the one-year rental really delivered about six months of clean cash flow. Leaders, this is the kind of worst-case math we owe our sellers, and it is exactly the math an anxious agent skips to avoid an awkward conversation.

In a recent development, the larger point for the industry is this. Compliance-driven financing blocks are a growing reality, and they reward the agent who can diagnose, not just discount. The old reflex of lowering price until something moves does not clear a building-level obstacle, and agents who only know that one move will lose listings they could have saved. The professionals who win in this environment are the ones who can look a seller in the eye and say, the problem is not your price, the problem is your building, and here is the plan to fix it.

Recent findings suggest that that is the advisor our clients actually need. Serve, don’t sell. In a market with this much noise, the agent who clings to a dying listing looks desperate, and the one who calmly takes the sign out of the yard, extends the agreement, and goes to fix the real problem looks like exactly what they are. The one in control.

In a recent development, darryl Davis, CSP, is a national speaker, real estate coach, and the bestselling author of How to Become a Power Agent® in Real Estate. Learn more at darrylspeaks.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a upcoming disclosure. This follows capital rotation out of Bitcoin products by a slew of traditional firms amid dwindling market sentiment.

Industry observers note that the bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways. In June, total assets were worth $90 million as it looked to diversify and grow holdings systematically.

It has been revealed that bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets. At the end of Q2, BTC holdings stood at $69.32 million but dropped slightly to above $61 million last quarter. The firm’s Ethereum exposure also dropped to $5 million.

However, Solana and XRP products filled the vacuum, highlighting institutional appetite for these assets. At the time of writing, the bank’s spot Solana ETF exposure is at $14.1 million after its investment in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF ballooned from seven shares to 875,407 shares.

Intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The company’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

More broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

Historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

The former have the potential to record spikes within the red wave, like in 2022 before the approval of spot ETF products in the United States. These products opened up digital assets to a latest stash of traditional capital.

Intesa and other banks have since increased their crypto exposure, driven by the need to diversify assets and a broader adoption spree. Heightened institutional and retail interests pushed Bitcoin to an all-time high above $125k last year. Right now, BTC trades at $63,819, while Ethereum is slightly below $1,800.

Founder of Inc. 5000 education publisher sells 30% of Laprea Education to an Employee Stock Ownership Blueprint.

According to recent reports, ROCHESTER, N.Y., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Anna DiGilio, a former second-grade teacher who founded Laprea Education Inc. in 2019, has sold 30% of the tech giant to an Employee Stock Ownership Initiative (ESOP). The transaction, which closed July 1, 2026, makes 25 eligible employees beneficial owners of the literacy publishing and education technology company at no cost to them. DiGilio will continue to lead the company as CEO.

Sources indicate that "After a cancer diagnosis made me think hard about what happens to this company without me, I realized I wanted the people who built it to own its future," noted DiGilio. "So I sold, not to a private equity firm, but to our teachers, curriculum writers, warehouse staff, and customer support team. When the owners are the people doing the work, children stay first in every decision.".

It has been revealed that "I've always cared deeply about the work we do, but knowing I now have a personal stake in the company's future makes it even more meaningful," said Tricia Martineck, digital accounts manager at Laprea. "It's exciting to be part of something that's growing while making a difference in the lives of children.".

DiGilio taught second grade for 23 years before founding Laprea. The organization now serves more than 800 school districts in all 50 states, employs about 50 people, and was named to the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies in 2025 and 2026. DiGilio was also named to the 2026 Inc. Female Founders 500.

Industry observers note that laprea's flagship line, Developing Decoders, includes more than 1,200 fiction and nonfiction decodable books written to align with popular phonics programs. The tech giant also publishes Teacher in a Backpack take-home literacy kits, hands-on phonics tools, and professional development for teachers, and has donated more than 256,000 books to children in the United States, Kenya, and Zimbabwe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot demonstrates its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

In a recent development, blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham says those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

In a recent development, the FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

According to recent reports, it demonstrates how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own owners. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

In a recent development, binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

In a recent development, while the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now reveals:.

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:.

Industry observers note that why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:.

Asset | Held with third-party custodians.

According to recent reports, the striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Sources indicate that compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, highlighted BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:.

Not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

Sources indicate that how Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:.

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

Recent findings suggest that what the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance states the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest patch says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:.

Sources indicate that the design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

It has been revealed that what it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

According to recent reports, what customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

Shiba Inu’s layer-2 network, Shibarium, is experiencing a major slowdown as daily network activity has fallen to three-digit figures (fewer than 1,000 transactions), hitting lows not seen in months.

Shibarium processed 546 transactions, according to Shibariumscan data, marking a slower period for the layer-2 network after activity spiked to a high of 6,370 on October 31, 2026. Transaction activity declined afterward, and the decline intensified amid the sell-off that hit the market in recent weeks.

The latest figures suggest that fewer transactions are taking place across Shibarium compared with periods of stronger activity. The key question now is whether Shibarium can regain momentum in the coming weeks.

Meanwhile, development continues behind the scenes for the Shiba Inu layer-2 network, as long-time Shiba Inu community member and developer Mazrael revealed a massive batch of contracts deployed on Puppynet, Shibarium's testnet.

But in the meantime, Shibarium’s fall to three-digit activity levels is a major slowdown that SHIB holders and ecosystem watchers will be watching closely.

Shiba Inu's on-chain holders increased as the number of wallets holding SHIB hit 1,700,930 on November 19, 2026.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 upcoming on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

The month of November has also seen consistent growth, with SHIB adding 4,520 holders since the start of the month. The broader 2026 trend is even more pronounced, with the number of holders of the token increasing by 152,300 since the beginning of the year.

While Shiba Inu's latest milestone seems remarkable, Mazrael suggested that the Shib ecosystem, including Shibarium, might have more holders than indicated, with 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on the BNB Chain.

"Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.
